scenes.tts: Michael Berridge worked on blowfly salivary glands. He showed that I P three appears within seconds of the hormone arriving. Eight years earlier, Robert Michell had proposed that breaking down inositol lipids is how receptors raise calcium. But a hormone starts many things at once. Did I P three raise the calcium, or did some third event?

scenes.tts: To test it, you need I P three inside a cell with no hormone outside. But I P three is too charged to cross a membrane. So the cell has to be opened. In Irene Schulz's laboratory in Frankfurt, H. Streb permeabilized pancreatic acinar cells. That makes the plasma membrane leaky to small molecules, while the compartments inside stay sealed.

scenes.visual: A cell with an internal store and mitochondria; the hormone is crossed out outside. IP3 bounces off the intact membrane; holes open in the wall; the compartments inside are outlined as sealed.

scenes.tts: Robin Irvine had prepared I P three in England, from human red blood cells. It was added to the opened cells. No hormone was added. Calcium came out of an internal store, and that store was not the mitochondria.

scenes.visual: IP3 with Irvine's tag drifts through a hole into the cell, hormone still crossed out. Calcium dots stream from the internal store into the cytosol; the mitochondria stay empty and are marked as not the source.
scenes.narration: Robin Irvine had prepared IP3 in England, from human red blood cells. It was added to the opened cells. No hormone was added. Calcium came out of an internal store, and that store was not the mitochondria.

scenes.tts: So I P three was sufficient without a hormone. Later work identified the store as the endoplasmic reticulum, and the target as the I P three receptor. This channel is built of four subunits, and it opens when I P three binds. The store holds free calcium at a thousand times the resting level or more, so an open channel means a fast rise.

scenes.visual: The store becomes the endoplasmic reticulum, full of calcium; a four-subunit channel in its wall; IP3 binds, the channel opens, calcium rises in the cytosol above.
